name: terminal-animation
title: Terminal Animation
description: A fake terminal window with traffic-light dots and tabs for commands like new, dev, test and build. It retypes the command for the chosen tab, then prints its coloured output line by line behind a blinking cursor.
use: A landing page or portfolio wants to show a product or developer workflow inside a familiar terminal.
avoid: The window forces a dark surface that clashes on light pages, and each tab's output text is written into the source.
a11y: The tab list and output log are labelled for screen readers, but tabs are not tied to a panel and the slide-up ignores reduced-motion. (keyboard: yes, labels: good, reduced motion: not handled)
looks: A dark rounded terminal window with three coloured dots and a row of six text tabs at the top, filled with a large monospaced command line and output lines. It floats on a violet-to-indigo gradient backdrop that darkens toward the edges.
behaves: Picking a tab retypes that tab's command character by character, then reveals its output lines one after another with timed pauses; the cursor blinks while typing and disappears once output finishes. The whole window also slides up into place when it first scrolls into view.
customise: Pass a tabs array of label, command and coloured lines; active tab, background image, forced dark and cursor hiding are props. Window styling and layout are file edits.
weight: light: A few dozen text lines revealed by timers; no canvas or heavy loop.
demo: Tabs new, dev, lint, fmt, test, build showing Vite scaffolding, server, lint and test output.
issues: Every frame crops the terminal window at the bottom, so its full height and output are never seen.
Frame 5 catches the reset between tabs and shows an almost empty window.
polishWhy: Typed commands and coloured output sell the effect; the recording never shows the window whole.

frames.note: The terminal window runs past the bottom edge of every frame, so its lower half is never shown.
